description.narrative:
Stödet till TWAS syftar till att stärka och främja vetenskaplig forskning inom basvetenskaper i utvecklingsländer; stärka utvecklingsländers egen forskningskapacitet; samt bygga upp hållbara forskningsmiljöer i utvecklingsländer med syfte att uppnå en kritisk massa av högt kvalificerade och innovativa forskare.
Det planerade stödet till TWAS (2022-2026) består av fyra delar: - Forskarstöd (TWAS Research Giants) - Regionala Partners (TWAS Regional Partners) - Vetenskapsdiplomati (Science Diplomacy Programme) - Forskarutbildning i klimat (PhD Programme for Climate Research) Sida ger ett stöd till genomförandet av programmen, kommunikation och information samt uppföljning och utvärdering.

Beredningen omfattar ett stöd till Unescos program ”The World Academy of Sciences for the advancement of science in developing countries (TWAS)”, för forskarutbildning och vetenskapsdiplomati med högst SEK 143,000,000 under perioden 1 mars 2022 - 31 december 2026.
TWAS övergripande mål och uppdrag är att bidra till att utvecklingsländer har tillräcklig vetenskaplig kapacitet och ledarskap för att ta itu med kritiska hållbarhetsutmaningar och engagera sig i internationella vetenskapliga initiativ som fullvärdiga och jämlika partners. Det ligger i linje med Sveriges strategi för forskningssamarbete och forskning inom utvecklingssamarbetet där Sida ska arbeta för en ökad förmåga hos samarbetsländer och regionala forskningsaktörer att planera, genomföra och använda forskning i kampen mot fattigdom.

The preparation includes support for UNESCO's program "The World Academy of Sciences for the advancement of science in developing countries (TWAS)", for postgraduate education and science diplomacy with a maximum of SEK 143,000,000 during the period 1 March 2022 - 31 December 2026.
TWA's overall goal and mission is to contribute to developing countries having sufficient scientific capacity and leadership to address critical sustainability challenges and engage in international scientific initiatives as full and equal partners. This is in line with Sweden's strategy for research collaboration and research in development collaboration, where Sida will work for an increased ability of partner countries and regional research actors to plan, implement and use research in the fight against poverty.

The World Academy of Sciences for the advancement of science in developing countries (TWAS) supports sustainable prosperity through research, education, policy and diplomacy. TWAS, founded in 1993, is a programme unit within the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) based in Trieste, Italy.
The key activities of TWAS include:
- Promoting excellence in scientific research, primarily in basic sciences (biology, chemistry, mathematics, physics and related fields) through research grants, fellowships, and awards to young scientists in countries that are still developing in science and technology;
- Supporting scientific capacity building through offering opportunities for scientists to share their expertise, participate in training programmes and attend international conferences;
- Promoting South-South and South-North cooperation in science, technology and innovation; and
- Advocating for science by influencing policy and promote the importance of science for solving major challenges facing developing countries.
TWAS has identified 66 developing countries in which capacity in science and technology is significantly lagging (https://twas.org/66-countries). The list includes the 45 least developed countries identified by the United Nations, to which 21 other countries were added because of their low-income levels and specific needs for support in building research capacity. TWAS sets these as priority countries for support, and since 2017, many TWAS research grants are reserved for scientists in these countries.
Sida has supported TWAS since 1991 and is today together with the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation the main funder of TWAS.
Examples of results:
Research and Project Grants: In 2024, TWAS relaunched its Research Grants programme after a stop in 2023 due to Sida's budget cuts. The programme comprises grants for individual scientists, research groups and collaborative interdisciplinary research involving one female and one male researcher of which at least one from a least-developed country. The call received a total of 437 applications of which 26 were awarded with Sida funding and an additional 16 grants with funds from the German Ministry of Research and Education. Sida-funded grants included both individual (15), group (7) and collaborative (4) grants with most grants awarded in the field of biology (12) followed by physics (8), chemistry (5) and mathematics (1).
In 2024, TWAS Research Grant awardees published 35 articles in international journals.
TWAS-Sida PhD Scholarships for Climate Research for Students from Least-Developed Countries: In 2021, TWAS proposed to Sida to build a cohort of climate experts in least-developed countries through PhD scholarships and a call for applications was set up and opened in 2022. The call received 456 applications and 13 scholarships could be awarded to seven female and six male fellows from 11 African countries (Benin, Chad, Ethiopia, Gambia, Lesotho, Malawi, Mali, Niger, Senegal, Tanzania, Togo) and two countries in Asia (Bangladesh and Nepal). During 2023 and 2024, all PhD students were able to start their scholarships with assistance from TWAS working at host institutions in Africa, Asia, Europe and North America. The programme involves south-south and south-north collaborations and applies for some students the "sandwich model" of PhD training (e.g. Ethiopia-Austria, Nepal-Bangladesh, Ghana-Singapore, Malawi-USA, Tanzania-Kenya).
The support from Sida also facilitated additional support by the Packard Foundation that resulted in collaboration with the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and development of the Joint Climate Science Network, Mentorship and Capacity Growth Programme. A training workshop with 15 IPCC experts and 45 students (TWAS students supported by Sida and IPCC students) from 36 developing countries was held in Trieste in May 2024.
Science Diplomacy Training: The 11th TWAS-AAAS (American Association for the Advancement of Science) Summer Course on Science Diplomacy took place in Trieste in June 2024. Science diplomacy refers to the use of scientific cooperation and exchanges to foster international relations and address global and regional challenges.
The TWAS-AAAS course was open for pairs consisting of an early-career scientist matching a decision maker (e.g. a local or national government official, diplomat, civil servant, representative of a research funding institution, staff or expert working for and/or with an international organization) preferably from the same country. The course received applications from 407 pairs for participation of which 10 where selected. Course participants received a deep education on how science and diplomacy intertwine to ease tensions and create lasting international bonds. The pairs were also challenged to play out roles in simulated negotiations on difficult topics with competing interests.
